column1: # Descriptions, limits, clean-up and rules for the value-object models, carried over from schema-model 0.2.0's
# hand-written models (ValueObjects) for every model and field that still exists. Java checks values first;
# these describe the result and must agree with it (ValueObjectLibraryTest checks realistic values).

column5: value
Canonical case-insensitive username, independent of the user's stable ID.
3 to 64 characters of letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit; stored lower-case.
TRIM,LOWERCASE
Case-insensitive email identity with unquoted mailbox syntax; ownership is not verified and provider aliases are never rewritten.
local@domain, stored lower-case, at most 254 characters; the local part is at most 64 characters and the domain is a valid DomainName (an internationalised domain is stored in its ASCII form).
TRIM,LOWERCASE
A person's name: a first name and an optional middle and last name.
Letters, single spaces, hyphens and apostrophes, starting with a letter; 1 to 50 characters, trimmed.
TRIM,COLLAPSE_SPACES
Letters, single spaces, hyphens and apostrophes, starting with a letter; 1 to 50 characters, trimmed.
TRIM,COLLAPSE_SPACES,BLANK_TO_ABSENT
Letters, single spaces, hyphens and apostrophes, starting with a letter; 1 to 50 characters, trimmed.
TRIM,COLLAPSE_SPACES,BLANK_TO_ABSENT
A phone number in E.164 form: a country calling code and a national number.
The country calling code, 1 to 3 digits; '+', spaces and punctuation are dropped, so +63 is stored as 63.
DIGITS_ONLY
The national number, digits only; spaces, dashes and brackets are dropped.
DIGITS_ONLY
an E.164 number has at most 15 digits
A URL: text that parses as a URI with a scheme.
A URI with a scheme, such as https://example.com. The full java.net.URI syntax check is not repeated here.
TRIM
A physical address in any international format; only the country is required. Blank parts are left out, as the Java record turns them into null.
The street and number.
TRIM,BLANK_TO_ABSENT
TRIM,BLANK_TO_ABSENT
TRIM,BLANK_TO_ABSENT
The postal or ZIP code, as written.
TRIM,BLANK_TO_ABSENT
A Country constant; UNKNOWN when the country is not known.
TRIM,UPPERCASE
A second line, such as an apartment or suite.
TRIM,BLANK_TO_ABSENT
A monetary amount with its currency; never a floating-point number.
The amount. The Java value object rounds it half-even to the currency's decimal places (2 for most fiat currencies, 8 for BTC, ...); round it the same way before saving.
A percentage, where 100 is the whole: 25 means 25%.
The percentage, such as 12.5 for 12.5%, rounded half-even to four decimal places; it may be negative or above 100.
A wallet address on a coin's network.
The address text; its format is not checked.
TRIM,UPPERCASE
Geographic coordinates: a latitude and a longitude in degrees.
Degrees, from -90 to 90.
Degrees, from -180 to 180.
A postal or ZIP code whose format follows its country's rules.

Stored upper-case: 2 to 10 letters, digits, spaces and hyphens, in the country's format where PostalCode knows one (e.g. UNITED_STATES 12345 or 12345-6789, CANADA A1A 1A1, UNITED_KINGDOM SW1A 1AA, JAPAN 123-4567).
TRIM,UPPERCASE
The country whose format the code follows.
TRIM,UPPERCASE

A multi-label DNS name in lower-case ASCII; syntax only, not registration or DNS existence.
At least two labels, at most 253 characters, no trailing dot, a TLD that is not all digits; an internationalised name is stored in its ASCII (punycode) form.

An IPv4 address in dotted decimal form.
Four octets from 0 to 255 without leading zeros, such as 192.168.0.1.
TRIM
An IPv6 address, stored as eight groups the way InetAddress.getHostAddress() writes it.
Any IPv6 literal (2001:DB8::1, ::1, ...) is stored as eight groups of lower-case hexadecimal without leading zeros, such as 2001:db8:0:0:0:0:0:1. Zone suffixes such as %eth0 are not supported.
TRIM,IPV6_CANONICAL
